audience.programmeDescription: VU Criminology examines offending, victims, criminalization and society’s responses through criminological theory, law, psychology, sociology and empirical research. Its Dutch-language degree includes a group investigation with an individual thesis and an open minor period.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers one approach that combines criminal law, psychology, sociology and empirical research. Youth Resilience to Extremism provides a focused example of prevention, and media and history courses help students examine how inequality and criminal justice are represented.

curriculum.limitation: The Dutch-language degree has 60 EC of required study in each of the first two years. Year three includes 30 EC of open study and a 12 EC research unit within the required courses. The research unit normally follows both criminological methods courses and combines a group investigation with an individual thesis.

componentNotes.y3-03: The research unit follows quantitative and qualitative criminological methods.
componentNotes.y3-05: The 30 EC can include a minor or approved elective study. Forensic Criminology is one minor option.

GOSGATE102.text: Law, Society & Justice examines legal, social and normative perspectives on law. Students compare legal traditions and study public and private law, human rights, justice, social control and change, race and gender. Case briefs, demand letters and mock trials develop legal reasoning, while a family-law topic supports the design of a socio-legal research proposal.

GOSPHIL212.text: Ethics examines moral reasoning through historical and contemporary theories and close philosophical reading. Students study utilitarianism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics, alongside Nietzsche, Murdoch and Nagel. Reflection and research essays develop interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.

Topics include responsibility, force, armed conflict, international crime, human rights, economic relations and environmental protection, followed by self-determination, Third World approaches, compliance and treaty politics. Case exercises and a research podcast develop legal reasoning and critical analysis.

GOSSOCI311.text: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory studies civil society through critical, neo-functionalist and decolonial perspectives. Topics include trust, social capital, public spheres, solidarity, social movements and civil repair. An experience report connects engagement or observation to course concepts, while an individual project uses theoretical and empirical sources to analyse a civil-society organisation, movement or initiative.

An interdisciplinary podcast, policy brief and research dossier develop analysis, while reflection examines how assumptions shape inquiry.
